catalogue: Australian residential fire and smoke safety construction

objects.name: residential fire-safety construction system
objects.definition: The coordinated passive and active construction used to limit fire spread, protect separating elements and openings, and warn occupants in a Class 1 or associated Class 10 building.
functions: Limit fire spread between buildings and dwellings
Maintain protected wall and floor construction at openings and junctions
Detect fire products and warn occupants

ncc_references.relationship: Performance and Deemed-to-Satisfy routing for fire separation, separating construction, garage-top dwellings, alarms and evacuation lighting.

cad.pattern: Connected wall, floor, opening, penetration and alarm assemblies
cad.placement: Across fire-separation boundaries and occupied areas selected by the project path
cad.start: Footing, ground slab or protected zone boundary
cad.opening: Every opening retains its own protection or permitted exception
cad.load: Mixed structural, protective and warning roles

notes: Fire resistance, combustibility, group number and alarm compliance are performance metadata attached to physical products and assemblies; they are not standalone geometry.

objects.name: fire-resisting external wall assembly
objects.definition: An external wall, including its framing or masonry, linings, cladding, junctions and protected openings, constructed for the required fire exposure where separation distances trigger protection.
functions: Limit fire spread to or from a nearby boundary or building
Carry its documented structural actions
Coordinate roof, eaves and opening terminations

cad.pattern: Continuous protected wall field over only the rule-triggered extent
cad.placement: At external walls within the applicable distance of a fire source feature
cad.start: Footing or ground slab unless another permitted start applies
cad.end: Documented roof or non-combustible eaves termination
cad.opening: Uses a permitted protected-opening assembly or explicit exception
cad.load: Structural wall whose fire performance belongs to the whole assembly

notes: The separation-distance zone is a spatial constraint; the physical wall assembly occupies the resulting wall extent.

objects.name: fire-resisting separating wall assembly
objects.definition: A continuous wall assembly separating Class 1 buildings, or a Class 1 building from a non-associated Class 10a building, including its full base-to-roof extent and all junction and service details.
functions: Limit fire spread between separate occupancies or buildings
Maintain separation through roof and veneer junctions
Control openings, services and combustible crossings

cad.pattern: Unbroken wall route following the occupancy boundary
cad.placement: Between the classified spaces that require separation
cad.end: Underside of non-combustible roof covering or documented projection above combustible covering
cad.opening: Restricts openings and requires service-specific fire protection
cad.load: May be loadbearing or non-loadbearing according to the tested or masonry construction

notes: Party wall and intertenancy wall are common search terms but can also be used for acoustic, title-boundary or higher-class building systems; building classification and construction path remain explicit.

objects.name: masonry fire-separating wall assembly
objects.definition: A separating wall formed from a continuous masonry leaf or leaves with mortar joints, supports, junctions and opening protection, using the applicable masonry construction path.
functions: Provide robust fire separation
Carry loads where designed as loadbearing masonry
Receive compatible firestop and roof-junction details

cad.pattern: Continuous bonded masonry courses over the separating-wall route
cad.placement: On a supporting footing, slab or beam
cad.opening: Built around scheduled openings and sealed service holes

notes: The existing masonry ontology supplies units, mortar, reinforcement and opening members; this object records their role as one complete fire-separating assembly.

objects.name: lightweight fire-separating wall assembly
objects.definition: A tested framed separating wall made from specified studs, tracks, cavities, fire-resistant lining layers, fixings, joints, seals and junction details.
functions: Provide tested fire separation at lower mass than masonry
Coordinate acoustic and structural requirements
Maintain the tested build-up at edges and services

cad.pattern: Framing grid with explicit lining layers and staggered joints
cad.placement: Along a required separating-wall route
cad.opening: Uses only service and opening details supported by evidence
cad.load: Loadbearing condition must match the tested or assessed system

notes: Non-uniform scaling, deleting a lining layer or moving studs can invalidate the referenced tested system.

objects.name: fire-resisting separating floor assembly
objects.definition: A floor and ceiling or soffit build-up whose structure, protective underside, supports, edge junctions and service openings collectively provide the documented fire separation.
functions: Limit vertical fire spread
Support occupied floor loads
Protect combustible or metal floor members from below where required

cad.pattern: Layered floor field with protected underside and explicit support grid
cad.placement: Between spaces requiring vertical fire separation
cad.opening: Every service and access opening retains a tested or permitted protection detail
cad.load: Structural floor plus passive protective layers

objects.name: garage-top dwelling fire-separation assembly
objects.definition: The walls, separating floor, protected ceiling or soffit, supporting elements and service treatments between a garage-top dwelling and a non-associated private garage.
functions: Separate a dwelling from the specified garage below or beside it
Protect the floor structure from garage-side fire exposure
Coordinate the jurisdiction-specific alarm requirements
attributes: heat alarm and notice where applicable

cad.pattern: Protected enclosure around the relevant garage-to-dwelling interfaces
cad.placement: Between the garage-top dwelling and non-associated garage
cad.end: Separating floor and enclosing wall junctions
cad.opening: Service openings retain fire protection and jurisdictional details
cad.load: Combines supporting construction and protective layers

notes: The NSW variation changes wall, floor and heat-alarm details; jurisdiction must be selected before generating the assembly.

objects.name: fire-protected horizontal projection assembly
objects.definition: A balcony, floor, verandah, soffit or similar horizontal projection at a separating wall, including its protected underside, supporting members and wall continuation.
functions: Limit fire spread around the end of a separating wall
Protect the underside and incorporated beams
Maintain separation at the wall-to-projection junction

cad.pattern: Horizontal protected field centred on the separating-wall projection
cad.placement: Where a horizontal projection forms part of the separating construction
cad.end: Required extent on the other side
cad.opening: Penetrations cannot reduce the documented performance

objects.name: common roof-space fire-separation assembly
objects.definition: A vertical non-combustible separation and its supports, joints and perimeter packing within an eave, verandah or similar space open to a roof space shared by more than one dwelling.
functions: Divide a common open roof or eaves space
Continue separation above wall and ceiling lines
Close perimeter gaps without creating weathering defects

cad.pattern: Vertical sheet barrier following the dwelling separation into open roof space
cad.placement: Within common eave, verandah or roof spaces
cad.opening: Crossings are explicit and limited by the selected path

notes: Cavity barrier is broader terminology; this object records the specific non-combustible vertical lining described by the Housing Provisions.

objects.name: separating-wall-to-roof fire termination
objects.definition: The detailed top junction where a separating or fire-resisting external wall meets the roof covering, eaves lining, fascia, gutter or flashing and every residual gap is closed as required.
functions: Stop fire bypassing the wall at the roof junction
Close profile and construction gaps
Preserve roof drainage and weatherproofing

cad.pattern: Continuous line following the wall head beneath or above the roof
cad.placement: At the wall-to-roof interface
cad.opening: Roof profiles and permitted crossings are individually closed or detailed
cad.load: Junction protection, weathering and support roles remain separate

objects.name: separating-wall-to-masonry-veneer fire closure
objects.definition: The mineral-fibre or other suitable fire-resisting closure in the gap between a separating wall and an external masonry veneer, arranged with the weatherproofing layers.
functions: Close the fire path at the wall-to-veneer junction
Maintain separation continuity
Preserve drainage and weatherproofing

cad.pattern: Vertical packed strip at the end of the veneer cavity
cad.placement: Between the separating-wall edge and external masonry veneer
cad.opening: Coordinates flashings and does not block required drainage

objects.name: fire-resisting wall opening-protection assembly
objects.definition: A complete window, door or other permitted construction installed in an opening through a fire-resisting external wall, including frame, leaf or glazing, closer, seals, fixings and perimeter interface.
functions: Protect the wall opening against fire spread
Retain normal opening or daylight function where permitted
Connect the protected product to the surrounding wall

cad.pattern: One protected product fitted into each scheduled opening
cad.placement: Within the fire-resisting external wall extent
cad.opening: Occupies and protects the wall opening
cad.load: Product and perimeter connections carry their documented actions

notes: Part 9.2 alternatives and tested fire-resistant doorsets use different evidence; opening protection must retain the selected route.

objects.name: non-openable fire window assembly
objects.definition: A fixed, non-openable window product with documented fire resistance, comprising its frame, fire-resistant glazing, retention, seals, fixings and wall perimeter detail.
functions: Transmit light while protecting a wall opening
Remain fixed closed
Maintain the documented integrity performance of the opening

cad.pattern: Fixed framed glazed unit
cad.placement: In a permitted fire-resisting external-wall opening
cad.opening: Fills the wall opening without an opening sash
cad.load: Glazing and frame reactions transferred through documented fixings

notes: Visible wire in glass does not prove the complete window has the required fire resistance.

objects.name: self-closing solid-core fire-separation door assembly
objects.definition: The Housing Provisions external-wall opening alternative made from a solid-core door leaf of the required construction, frame, hinges, latch and a device that returns the leaf to closed position.
functions: Protect a permitted doorway through the external wall
Close automatically after use
Provide normal pedestrian access

cad.pattern: One hinged leaf and closer within a fixed frame
cad.placement: In a permitted external-wall opening
cad.opening: Leaf swing remains clear and closer returns it shut
cad.load: Leaf supported by hinges and frame

notes: This is kept separate from a fire-resistant doorset tested and installed under its own standard.

objects.name: fire-resistant doorset
objects.definition: A tested fire-resistant door assembly supplied and installed as a coordinated leaf, frame, hardware, seals, fixings, wall interface and identification system.
functions: Protect a trafficable opening in fire-resistant construction
Close and latch as documented
Maintain traceable tested or assessed performance
materials: intumescent and smoke seals where required

cad.pattern: Scheduled tested doorset fitted as one product assembly
cad.placement: In fire-resistant wall construction where selected by the project path
cad.opening: Protects the doorway when closed
cad.load: Leaf and hardware reactions transferred to tested frame and wall

notes: Included as a broader building object and supporting standard family; it is not silently substituted for the Part 9.2 solid-core door alternative.

objects.name: hollow glass-block opening assembly
objects.definition: A non-openable translucent infill panel built from hollow glass blocks, joints, perimeter channels or reinforcement and seals within a permitted external-wall opening.
functions: Transmit diffuse light
Permanently enclose a small permitted opening
Connect the block panel to the surrounding wall

cad.pattern: Regular grid of hollow glass blocks and joints
cad.placement: In a permitted non-habitable-room external-wall opening
cad.opening: Permanently fills the wall opening
cad.load: Panel supported at base and restrained at perimeter

objects.name: passive firestop system
objects.definition: The tested or assessed combination of opening, host wall or floor, penetrating service or joint, firestop products, supports, fixings and identification that restores the required fire separation.
functions: Limit passage of flame and hot gases through discontinuities
Control heat transfer where the selected system provides it
Maintain movement or service function within the tested configuration

cad.pattern: One evidence-linked system instance at each service opening or linear joint
cad.placement: At discontinuities in a fire-resistant wall, floor or covering
cad.opening: Fills, closes or reacts within the exact opening geometry
cad.load: Non-structural protection with required service support

notes: Product colour and firestop branding do not establish a system. Host, service, size, orientation, product depth, backing, supports and evidence must match.

objects.name: service-penetration firestop assembly
objects.definition: A passive firestop system around one or more pipes, cables, conduits, ducts or mixed services passing through a fire-resistant wall or floor.
functions: Close the service opening
Accommodate the documented service behaviour in fire
Connect the firestop products to the host construction

cad.pattern: Discrete protected opening centred on each service group
cad.placement: Through the separating wall, floor or protective covering
cad.opening: Surrounds and closes the service penetration
cad.load: Firestop is not the primary service support unless the system says so

objects.name: linear-joint firestop assembly
objects.definition: A tested fire-resistant joint system extending along a construction, control or movement gap between fire-resistant elements, including backing, fill, seal and edge preparation.
functions: Maintain separation along a continuous gap
Accommodate documented movement
Seal irregular interfaces between adjacent elements

cad.pattern: Continuous protected line following the joint route
cad.placement: Between adjacent fire-resistant elements
cad.opening: Fills the designed gap without rigidly bridging required movement
cad.load: Flexible closure, not structural load transfer

objects.name: electrical-box fire-protection assembly
objects.definition: The framed recess, electrical box, surrounding or rear mineral-fibre packing, firestop pad or hood and lining repair used where a switch, socket or outlet is installed in a hollow separating wall.
functions: Protect the recessed service opening
Limit direct paths between opposite wall faces
Retain the electrical accessory and lining continuity
materials: putty pad or fire hood where tested

cad.pattern: One protected framed recess behind each affected electrical accessory
cad.placement: Within a hollow separating wall
cad.opening: Encloses the electrical-box recess and cable entries
cad.load: Accessory supported by local framing or box fixing

notes: The Housing Provisions prescriptive packing detail and a separately tested putty-pad or hood system are alternative paths, not interchangeable parts.

objects.name: structural fire-protection system
objects.definition: A selected board enclosure, spray, intumescent coating or encasement applied around a structural member as a complete evidence-backed system with preparation, fixings and finishes.
functions: Limit heating of the structural member
Maintain required structural adequacy for the documented period
Protect the treatment from service exposure where required

cad.pattern: Continuous protective envelope following the structural member
cad.placement: Around a steel, timber, concrete or composite member requiring protection
cad.opening: Maintains continuity at brackets, connections and service clashes
cad.load: Protection does not replace the structural member

notes: Included for whole-building reuse; the house-scale Housing Provisions commonly resolve walls and floors as complete systems rather than specifying a generic structural coating.

objects.name: domestic interconnected alarm system
objects.definition: The coordinated set of smoke alarms and any permitted heat alarms, mounting bases, power supplies, backup batteries, interconnects, controls, warning devices and required notices within one dwelling or relevant garage arrangement.
functions: Detect smoke or heat according to the selected alarm type
Warn occupants throughout the connected system
Continue operating through the documented backup arrangement

cad.pattern: Distributed alarm devices connected as one dwelling system
cad.placement: On or near ceilings in required bedroom, hallway and storey zones
cad.end: Last compatible alarm or warning node
cad.opening: Respects dead-air spaces and ceiling obstructions
cad.load: Light device loads supported by ceiling or wall substrate

notes: Interconnection is a system relationship; a wireless radio link is not itself modelled as a solid cable, though its physical module is.

objects.name: Class 1b smoke-alarm-activated evacuation-lighting system
objects.definition: The smoke-alarm-activated lighting serving the relevant Class 1b corridor, hallway or area, provided either by a light within the alarm or by connected fixed lighting.
functions: Illuminate the evacuation route after alarm activation
Coordinate detection and lighting controls
Use existing or dedicated luminaires without premature switch-off
not_synonyms: normal corridor light without alarm activation

cad.pattern: Alarm trigger linked to luminaires covering the evacuation route
cad.placement: In Class 1b corridors, hallways or areas required by the selected path
cad.opening: Light distribution avoids obstructions
cad.load: Electrical fittings supported by ceilings or walls

notes: This is the Housing Provisions Class 1b arrangement, not a generic substitution for AS/NZS 2293 emergency lighting in other building classes.

objects.name: fire-resistant plasterboard lining
objects.definition: A gypsum plasterboard sheet manufactured for use as one or more specified layers in a tested fire-resistant wall, ceiling, soffit, column or beam system.
functions: Delay heat and flame passage through the assembly
Provide a finishable sheet surface
Protect framing or structural members when installed in the documented layer build-up

cad.pattern: Large sheets laid in one or more staggered layers
cad.placement: Fixed to the documented framing or substrate
cad.opening: Cut and protected only as the tested detail permits
cad.load: Non-structural lining unless the tested system assigns bracing or other roles

notes: Fire-rated is often applied loosely to the sheet; the assembly, including number of layers, joints, fixings and supports, carries the fire result.

objects.name: fire-separating shaftliner panel
objects.definition: A thick fire-resistant gypsum or composite panel captured in a proprietary stud-and-track wall system, commonly forming a central protective layer in lightweight separating construction.
functions: Provide a central fire-resistant barrier layer
Engage with shaftwall or party-wall framing profiles
Allow staged construction from one side where the selected system permits

cad.pattern: Vertical panels captured between compatible framing profiles
cad.placement: At the core of a documented lightweight separating-wall system
cad.opening: Uses system-specific framing and protection
cad.load: Protective panel supported by the wall framing system

objects.name: rigid fire-protection board
objects.definition: A rigid calcium-silicate, vermiculite, gypsum, fibre-cement or other tested board used to line or enclose construction for passive fire protection.
functions: Provide a protective board layer
Form enclosures around members or services
Receive tested joints and fixings

cad.pattern: Cut boards forming protective faces or box enclosures
cad.placement: On framing, around members or across tested openings
cad.opening: Uses documented cut-outs and joint protection
cad.load: Non-structural protective board unless otherwise documented

objects.name: fire-protective floor or beam underside covering
objects.definition: A continuous protective board, sheet or spray covering fixed beneath combustible or metal floor construction and incorporated beams to provide the selected fire-protection path.
functions: Shield floor members and beams from underside fire exposure
Create a continuous protected soffit
Coordinate joints and service openings

cad.pattern: Continuous protected underside field including beam returns
cad.placement: Below the floor, projection or incorporated beams
cad.opening: No unprotected service or access cuts
cad.load: Covering supported by documented framing or direct fixings

objects.name: non-combustible roof-space vertical lining
objects.definition: The vertical non-combustible sheet or panel that physically divides a common eave, verandah or similar space open to the roof space between dwellings.
functions: Form the visible or concealed separating plane
Close the open roof-space route
Receive perimeter packing and permitted crossing details

cad.pattern: Vertical panels cut to the underside roof profile
cad.placement: In the common open roof or eaves space
cad.opening: Cut tightly and packed around permitted crossings

objects.name: lightweight separating-wall frame
objects.definition: The selected studs, tracks, noggings, clips and local opening members that support lining layers and maintain the geometry of a tested lightweight separating wall.
functions: Support wall linings
Transfer wall loads
Maintain cavities, joints and clearances required by the selected system

cad.pattern: Repeated studs between base and head tracks with system-specific clips
cad.placement: Within the lightweight separating-wall thickness
cad.opening: Uses tested jamb, head and sill framing
cad.load: Structural or non-structural according to tested wall system

objects.name: separating-wall cavity
objects.definition: A deliberate clear or insulated space between wall leaves, framing rows or lining layers in a fire-separating wall, bounded by the tested assembly and interrupted only by documented components.
functions: Separate wall leaves
Accommodate insulation or limited services where permitted
Contribute to acoustic and fire behaviour of the tested system

cad.pattern: Continuous void between separated wall leaves
cad.placement: Within the tested wall thickness
cad.opening: Preserves required clearances around documented components

notes: A cavity is physical modelled space but carries no fire rating by itself.

objects.name: separating-wall mineral-wool insulation
objects.definition: Mineral-wool batts or slabs installed within a separating wall or floor cavity as the product, density, thickness and fit specified by the selected tested system.
functions: Contribute to documented acoustic and thermal performance
Support the tested fire behaviour where included
Fill the designated cavity without unapproved gaps or compression

cad.pattern: Repeated batts filling scheduled framing bays
cad.placement: Within wall or floor cavities
cad.opening: Fitted around documented services without unapproved voids
cad.load: Non-structural insulation supported by friction or retaining components

objects.name: mineral-fibre fire-resisting gap packing
objects.definition: Mineral fibre or another documented fire-resisting material compressed or fitted into a construction gap to close a fire path while accommodating the junction geometry.
functions: Close irregular or linear gaps
Limit flame and hot-gas bypass
Back up another seal or finish where the selected detail requires
materials: ceramic or other documented mineral fibre

cad.pattern: Continuous packed strips or discrete packed annuli
cad.placement: Inside construction gaps and firestop openings
cad.opening: Conforms to the gap without blocking required drainage or movement

objects.name: top-of-wall fire-resisting packing
objects.definition: The mineral-fibre or other suitable fire-resisting packing closing the residual gap between the top of a separating wall and the underside of a non-combustible roof covering or protected construction.
functions: Close the wall-head fire path
Conform to roof profiles
Maintain continuity without unapproved combustible infill

cad.pattern: Continuous packing cut or compressed to the roof underside profile
cad.placement: At the separating-wall head
cad.opening: Fitted around only permitted roof crossings

objects.name: masonry-veneer junction fire-resisting packing
objects.definition: The mineral-fibre or other suitable fire-resisting packing installed vertically between a separating-wall end and the external masonry veneer while retaining weatherproofing and drainage paths.
functions: Close the wall-end cavity fire path
Connect the separating plane to the outer masonry leaf
Coordinate flashing and cavity drainage

cad.pattern: Continuous vertical packed strip at wall end
cad.placement: Between separating wall and masonry veneer
cad.opening: Coordinates rather than blocks required weather drainage

objects.name: electrical-box cavity fire-resisting packing
objects.definition: Mineral fibre or other suitable fire-resisting material packed into the locally framed cavity immediately behind an electrical switch, socket or outlet in a hollow separating wall.
functions: Close the cavity behind the recessed electrical box
Limit direct fire passage through the hollow wall
Support the Housing Provisions prescriptive outlet detail where applicable

cad.pattern: Dense local infill behind the electrical box
cad.placement: Inside the framed cavity surrounding the recessed accessory
cad.opening: Fits around cable entries without leaving an open cavity route

objects.name: fire-resistant lining joint tape
objects.definition: Paper, glass-fibre or other documented tape embedded across joints in fire-resistant board linings as part of the selected joint-treatment system.
functions: Reinforce board joints
Hold joint compound across sheet edges
Maintain the documented lining finish and fire-system continuity

cad.pattern: Continuous narrow strips centred over scheduled sheet joints
cad.placement: Embedded in compatible joint compound
cad.opening: Continues around protected opening returns where documented

objects.name: fire-resistant lining joint compound
objects.definition: A compatible setting or drying compound applied with joint tape over board joints, fastener heads, corners and returns in a documented fire-resistant lining system.
functions: Fill and finish lining joints
Embed reinforcement tape
Complete the documented joint construction

cad.pattern: Tapered bands over sheet joints and local fastener spots
cad.placement: On the exposed face of documented lining layers
cad.opening: Finishes protected reveals without replacing perimeter firestop

objects.name: fire-and-acoustic perimeter sealant joint
objects.definition: A compatible flexible sealant joint at the perimeter, base, head, layer joint or small gap of a tested wall or ceiling system where both fire and acoustic continuity are documented.
functions: Seal air and sound leakage paths
Maintain perimeter continuity
Accommodate limited documented movement

cad.pattern: Continuous bead following tested wall and ceiling perimeters
cad.placement: Between lining edges and adjoining construction
cad.opening: Returns around openings only where documented

objects.name: fire-system lining screw
objects.definition: A steel screw of the type, length, gauge, head and corrosion protection specified to fasten a particular layer of fire-resistant lining to framing or furring.
functions: Hold protective boards to supports
Maintain layer spacing and edge restraint
Transfer board self-weight and service actions

cad.pattern: Repeated fasteners at documented edge and field spacing
cad.placement: Through lining into framing or furring
cad.opening: Additional fixings follow tested opening details

objects.name: fire-separation wall clip
objects.definition: A proprietary steel clip connecting leaves, shaftliner framing or adjacent structural frames in a lightweight separating-wall system while preserving the selected breakaway, movement or restraint behaviour.
functions: Locate wall leaves
Transfer only the documented restraint forces
Permit system-specific movement or breakaway response

cad.pattern: Discrete clips repeated at system-specific points
cad.placement: Between documented framing leaves or to supporting construction
cad.opening: Avoids unapproved bridging at openings
cad.load: Transfers only documented restraint or breakaway forces

objects.name: fire-separating wall deflection head
objects.definition: A head-track, stud-clearance, lining, slip, packing and seal arrangement allowing the structure above a fire-separating wall to deflect without crushing the wall or opening a fire path.
functions: Accommodate documented vertical movement
Maintain wall-head lateral restraint
Keep the fire and acoustic seal continuous

cad.pattern: Continuous head arrangement above repeated studs
cad.placement: Between wall top and deflecting structure
cad.opening: Coordinates heads over door and service openings
cad.load: Provides lateral restraint while allowing vertical movement

objects.name: fire-separating wall base track
objects.definition: The continuous steel channel or documented timber member locating separating-wall studs or shaftliner panels at their base and fixed through the selected perimeter seal to the support.
functions: Locate wall framing at the base
Transfer wall reactions to the support
Provide a straight edge for lining and base sealing

cad.pattern: Continuous channel following the wall base
cad.placement: On slab, footing, floor or beam support
cad.opening: Interrupted and framed only by tested opening details
cad.load: Transfers wall base reactions through anchors

objects.name: board structural-fire-protection enclosure
objects.definition: A box or profile-following enclosure of fire-protection boards, corner joints, supports, fixings and seals around a structural member or service.
functions: Create a continuous protective envelope
Hold the documented board distance and thickness
Protect member connections and discontinuities

cad.pattern: Continuous board box around member cross-section
cad.placement: Around protected beams, columns or other structural members
cad.opening: Returns around connections and only permits documented penetrations
cad.load: Enclosure self-weight supported independently or by documented attachments

objects.name: fire-protection board enclosure corner joint
objects.definition: The butt, rebate, mitre, overlapping or proprietary corner connection between fire-protection boards enclosing a structural member.
functions: Join adjacent enclosure faces
Maintain protective thickness at corners
Receive compatible fixing and joint treatment

cad.pattern: Continuous longitudinal corner along enclosure
cad.placement: At each meeting of enclosure faces
cad.opening: Returns around brackets and connections

objects.name: fire-protection board enclosure fixing
objects.definition: A steel screw, staple, pin, clip or angle fixing specified to hold fire-protection boards and support members in an enclosure.
functions: Retain protection boards
Connect support angles or channels
Maintain joint and corner geometry under service and fire conditions

cad.pattern: Repeated fixings along joints, edges and supports
cad.placement: Through boards or support profiles
cad.opening: Additional fixings follow connection returns
cad.load: Carries enclosure self-weight and service loads

objects.name: non-openable fire-window frame
objects.definition: The fixed tested perimeter frame, rebates, beads and anchors that supports fire-resistant glazing in a non-openable fire-window assembly.
functions: Support and retain fire-resistant glazing
Transfer glazing reactions to the wall
Form the perimeter interface and protected rebate

cad.pattern: Fixed perimeter and any tested internal divisions
cad.placement: Within the wall opening
cad.opening: No opening sash or hardware
cad.load: Transfers glazing and fire-test assembly reactions to wall

objects.name: fire-resistant glazing pane
objects.definition: A documented wired, laminated, gel-filled, ceramic or other fire-resistant transparent or translucent pane used within a tested opening-protection system.
functions: Transmit light or vision
Contribute the documented fire performance
Remain retained within the tested glazing frame and seals

cad.pattern: One pane or tested pane grid within fixed frame
cad.placement: Inside the fire-window glazing rebate
cad.opening: Permanently retained and non-openable
cad.load: Pane loads transferred through tested blocks and frame

notes: Fire resistance and human-impact safety are separate evidence fields even when one pane provides both.

objects.name: fire-resistant glazing seal
objects.definition: A tested gasket, tape, setting compound, intumescent liner or sealant between fire-resistant glazing and its frame or bead.
functions: Cushion and retain glass within the rebate
Close the glass-to-frame interface
React or remain stable as required by the tested system

cad.pattern: Continuous perimeter around each pane edge
cad.placement: Between pane and frame or bead
cad.opening: Follows all supported pane edges
cad.load: Cushions and seals; retention depends on complete frame system

objects.name: solid-core fire-separation door leaf
objects.definition: A hinged solid-core door leaf of the material, thickness and construction selected for the Housing Provisions protected-opening alternative.
functions: Close the doorway
Provide a robust solid barrier
Carry hinges, latch and closer forces

cad.pattern: Single rectangular hinged panel with hardware preparations
cad.placement: Within protected door frame
cad.opening: Rotates through scheduled swing

objects.name: protected-opening door closer
objects.definition: A surface-mounted, concealed, floor-spring or hinge-integrated mechanism that returns the protected door leaf to its closed position after opening.
functions: Close the door automatically
Control closing speed
Overcome latch and seal resistance where documented

cad.pattern: One closer mechanism per controlled leaf
cad.placement: At door head, hinge, floor or concealed location
cad.opening: Moves through door swing and returns leaf closed
cad.load: Applies controlled closing force to leaf

objects.name: protected-opening door frame
objects.definition: The fixed head, jambs, stops, anchors and perimeter interface supporting a solid-core protected-opening door or tested fire-resistant doorset.
functions: Support hinges, latch and closer reactions
Locate the closed leaf
Connect the door assembly to the fire-resisting wall

cad.pattern: Three-sided or documented four-sided fixed perimeter
cad.placement: Within the protected wall opening
cad.opening: Defines clear doorway and closed-leaf stop
cad.load: Transfers door hardware reactions to wall

objects.name: protected-opening door latch
objects.definition: A latch or lockset that holds a self-closing protected door leaf in its closed position without preventing normal release for egress.
functions: Retain the closed leaf
Engage the frame strike
Release through the documented handle or egress operation

cad.pattern: One latching set at the leaf closing edge
cad.placement: Between door leaf and frame strike
cad.opening: Releases and re-engages through door swing
cad.load: Retains closed leaf against pressure and seal forces

objects.name: hollow glass block
objects.definition: A factory-made translucent hollow glass masonry unit laid or assembled with matching units to fill a non-openable opening.
functions: Transmit diffuse light
Form a repeated panel field
Transfer self-weight through block joints

cad.pattern: Repeated modular grid units
cad.placement: Within the glass-block opening panel
cad.opening: Permanently fills its grid cell

objects.name: hollow glass-block joint
objects.definition: The mortar, spacer, sealant or proprietary channel joint separating and connecting hollow glass blocks within a panel and at its perimeter.
functions: Hold block spacing
Transfer local panel forces
Seal and finish the block grid

cad.pattern: Orthogonal grid lines between blocks and continuous perimeter
